---
title: "Settings"
description: >-
  Shortcuts, which attachment is previewed when an item has several, the contact sheet grid and page limit, annotations and EPUB rendering.
---

**Zotero → Settings → zotLook.**

## Shortcuts

Each action has one shortcut. Click the field, press the combination, and it
takes effect immediately — no restart.

The pane **warns beneath the row concerned** when a combination is already
taken, checking the main window's own keys, Zotero's configurable shortcuts,
and zotLook's other actions. The warning is not confined to the moment of
recording: it is still there the next time you open the settings, since a
collision that already exists would otherwise be invisible.

This is not cosmetic. If two zotLook actions carry the same combination, one of
them wins and the other never fires.

::: {.callout-important title="A clean result means less than it looks"}
It warns rather than refuses, deliberately. Zotero publishes no list of other
plugins' shortcuts, and the operating system publishes none at all. A clean
result therefore means *no conflict with Zotero* — not *free*.
:::

**Restore defaults** writes the shipped combinations back:

| Action | Default |
|---|---|
| Preview | Space |
| Notes | Shift+Space |
| Contact sheet | Ctrl+Shift+Space |
| Contact sheet in a window | Shift+Alt+Space |

## Combinations that never arrive

When the operating system or another application claims a combination, it takes
it **before** Zotero sees the keys. There is then nothing to detect: the
keystroke never arrives, and no list could be consulted for it — macOS gives up
only its own symbolic shortcuts, as undocumented numeric ids, with nothing at
all about what other programs have claimed, and Windows offers no query for
`RegisterHotKey` whatsoever.

That absence is itself a finding, though. Press such a combination while
recording and the modifier keys do arrive — they are ordinary key events — but
the key between them does not. Let go without anything having arrived and the
pane tells you so, rather than sitting on "press keys…" indefinitely. Choose a
different combination.

## Which attachment is previewed

Two modes:

- **By type** — a ranking you arrange yourself: PDF, EPUB, HTML, image, video,
  anything else. Drag an entry up or down with the buttons beside the list. It
  is a ranking rather than a filter, so nothing is ever excluded; the order only
  decides who wins when an item has several attachments.
- **First attachment** — whatever the item lists first, regardless of type.

## The contact sheet

**Columns** (default 5) decides the width of the grid. Fewer columns means
larger thumbnails, and the renderer raises the resolution to match, so they stay
sharp rather than being blown up.

**Page limit** (default 0, meaning no limit) caps how many pages are rendered.
It exists for unusually large scans, to bound how long generation may take and
how much temporary disk space it may use. When it bites, the sheet says so at
the bottom.

## Kept previews

Two of the things zotLook makes cost seconds to make: the contact sheet, which
draws every page of a book, and the EPUB preview, which unpacks the book and
reassembles it as one page. Both are kept and shown again.

**Keep converted previews and show them again** (default on) does that. What
was made once is shown unchanged until something that would make it the wrong
answer has changed — the file itself, its annotations, or the settings that
shape it, such as the contact sheet's column count.

Kept previews live in the profile's cache area rather than in your Zotero
library, so they are not backed up with it. The system's temporary area, the
obvious place for them, is the one place they cannot be: Zotero clears its own
temporary directory completely at every shutdown, and a preview kept there
never survived a restart. Switch it off if you would rather have the space:
everything is then made afresh on every call and nothing outlives the session.

The folder is called `zotLook-cache` and sits in the Zotero profile inside the
cache directory the system sets aside for this — under `AppData\Local` on
Windows, `~/Library/Caches` on macOS, and `~/.cache/zotero/zotero/<profile>` on
Linux. That is deliberate: anything that clears caches reaches it, and you may
delete the folder yourself while Zotero is closed. It costs no more than making
the previews again.

**Drop previews unused for** (default 30 days) clears up without your having to
think about it. It counts from the last *use* rather than from when the preview
was made: a book you open every week stays, one you looked at once in March
goes. The check runs when Zotero starts rather than while you work — a preview
vanishing mid-session would be more confusing than the space it occupied. A `0`
switches it off, and they then stay until you delete them yourself.

**Delete kept previews** throws them all away at once. Beside it stands what
they currently occupy — without that figure, pressing it would be a guess.
After the deletion it reads zero, and the next call makes them afresh.

::: {.callout-note title="What is not kept"}
The annotated copy of a PDF is made the same way but deliberately not kept: it
is a whole copy of the document, the largest thing here for the smallest
saving, since exporting it takes a moment where a contact sheet takes seconds.
It lives for the session and goes with the working directory at the next start.
:::

## Annotations

Zotero keeps annotations in its database rather than in the file, so a preview
of the stored document would show it unmarked. There is a switch per format,
both on by default, because the work behind them differs.

**Draw them into PDF previews and contact sheets** hands the work to Zotero: it
writes a copy with your highlights, notes, areas and ink drawn on the page, and
that copy is previewed. It costs a copy of the document, which is why it is
worth being able to switch off on its own.

**Mark them in EPUB previews** costs nothing worth naming, since the page is
being assembled anyway. There is no export for an EPUB, so zotLook reads the
position Zotero stored — an EPUB CFI, which names the chapter, the element and the exact
characters — and marks the page it builds accordingly: highlights filled in
their own colour, underlines drawn as underlines. A button in the corner of
the preview opens a list of every annotation in reading order — each quotation
marked as it is marked in the book, so an entry is recognisable at a glance —
with its comment; clicking an entry takes you to the passage. That is where notes live, which have no passage of their own, and
any position that no longer resolves because the book itself has changed
since.

Turn one off to preview that format as it is stored. Attachments that carry no
annotations are recognised before any work starts either way, so the settings
only matter for documents you have actually marked up.

## EPUB

**Render EPUBs into a preview page** is on by default, because no system
preview shows an EPUB on its own.

If you would rather use a preview extension of the operating system than the
one built into zotLook, switch zotLook's EPUB preview off here — the book then
goes to the panel untouched, like any other file. With no such extension
installed, EPUB attachments then have no preview at all.
